episode.title: This SPONGE Is NOT Supposed To REPEL WATER?!

synopsis: A man attempts to clean a surface with a sponge that, instead of absorbing liquid, actively repels and pushes water away from itself.
narration: Okay so, this old sponge, I swear, the water just refuses to stick to it. It’s like it has its own force field, pushing every drop away, making it impossible to clean.

shots.prompt: Close-up of Ihsan's hands, wearing a plain black crew-neck t-shirt, attempting to wipe a small puddle of spilled water on a worn wooden table with a common yellow sponge. The water visibly beads up and rolls off the sponge, refusing to be absorbed, creating a shimmering, impossible repulsion effect. The view stays in one unchanging position and angle for the whole shot.

Ihsan's hands, wearing a plain black crew-neck t-shirt, press the sponge down firmly into a larger puddle of water on the same wooden table. The water visibly pushes away from the sponge's surface, forming a clear, concave depression around it, rather than being absorbed. The frame never moves.

Medium shot of Ihsan's hands, wearing a plain black crew-neck t-shirt, attempting to submerge the sponge in a clear glass bowl filled with water on the wooden table. The sponge floats stubbornly on the surface, pushing a deep, visible depression into the water, as if an invisible force field is resisting its entry. The view stays in one unchanging position and angle for the whole shot.

Close-up of Ihsan's hands, wearing a plain black crew-neck t-shirt, holding the sponge directly under a thin stream of water from a tap, just off-frame. The water stream visibly diverts and splits around the sponge's impossible, water-repelling surface, not touching it at all. The frame never moves.

music: A sparse, dry, percussive bed built from soft, rapid 'plink' sounds like water droplets hitting a resistant surface, mixed with a low, sustained 'thrum' that subtly shifts pitch. There are no melody lines, no swells, no ethereal pads, and no vocals. The music opens with sound in its very first second, maintaining a slow, steady pulse and plenty of negative space.
